transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see us today?

I feel like I just can’t keep my projects organized anymore, no matter how many lists and calendars I use. It’s gotten really bad since I was promoted into a new role about two years ago, and I was recently put on a performance improvement plan because I'm struggling so much to keep up. I just feel completely overwhelmed trying to manage all the moving parts.
Do you often find yourself worrying about not meeting expectations or making mistakes in your new role, even when you're not actively working on projects?

Yes, I worry about it constantly, and the fear of letting people down is always on my mind now that I'm on a performance improvement plan. It’s incredibly distressing to lose my reputation as a reliable professional, so I spend my evenings anxious and re-reading documents late into the night. I dread going into the office and honestly never feel like I'm truly off the clock.
Have you started avoiding specific tasks or situations at work because they make you feel anxious or overwhelmed?

I don't really avoid my tasks; instead, I actually find myself spending long hours late at night trying to force myself to get through them. However, I have started dreading going into the office altogether because of the constant feeling that I'm letting people down.
Can you tell me more about what specifically happens when you're at the office that makes you dread going in, is it the interactions with colleagues, the fear of being evaluated, or something else?

It's the constant feeling that I'm letting my team down because my projects are falling behind schedule. I'm on a formal performance improvement plan because I keep losing track of details and bouncing between tasks, which makes being in the office incredibly stressful despite working late most nights to catch up.

Can you tell me if there was a specific traumatic or stressful event, such as a major change or incident, that occurred around the time your symptoms started or worsened, or if it's been more of a gradual increase in stress and anxiety over time?

It started when I was promoted to a client-facing sales strategist role about two years ago. Suddenly, I had to manage multiple complex campaigns and rapid task-switching, which completely overwhelmed the informal systems I used to rely on. Since then, it's been a steady, stressful struggle to keep up.
Did your difficulties with organization and feeling overwhelmed start immediately after the promotion, or was there a period where you seemed to adapt before things became unmanageable?

The difficulties started pretty much right away after the promotion. The sudden jump in cognitive load and rapid task-switching immediately strained the informal systems I had always used to keep myself on track. Since then, the problems have just been steadily getting worse over the last two years.

You mentioned that your difficulties with organization and feeling overwhelmed started right away after your promotion, but can you tell me if you've experienced any significant distress or impairment in social or other areas of life outside of work?

I haven't really thought about it or noticed any major issues in my social life. Honestly, all of my focus and energy have been entirely consumed by trying to keep up with the overwhelming stress at work.
Do you experience excessive and persistent worry about everyday things, not just related to your work performance, such as finances, health, or minor matters?

No, I don't really worry excessively about other everyday things like my finances, health, or minor household matters. My anxiety and stress are almost entirely focused on my work performance, keeping up with my projects, and the constant fear of letting my team down.
Can you describe how your anxiety and stress levels change when you're on vacation or completely disconnected from work-related tasks for an extended period?

To be honest, I haven't been able to take a proper vacation or fully disconnect from work recently, especially with the constant pressure of the performance improvement plan. Because of that, I'm not really sure how my stress levels would change in that kind of scenario.
Is your anxiety primarily triggered by the fear of not meeting work expectations and letting your team down, or are there other specific situations or thoughts that trigger your anxiety?

Yes, my anxiety is heavily tied to work and that constant fear of letting my team and supervisor down. Being on a performance improvement plan and always feeling behind makes me dread going in, even though I'm working late hours to try and keep up. It's especially hard because I've always prided myself on being a quiet, reliable professional.

Can you clarify if your anxiety is solely focused on work performance and the fear of letting your team down, or if you also experience significant anxiety related to other aspects of your life, such as social interactions or personal relationships?

Yes, my anxiety and dread are almost entirely tied to my work performance, the performance improvement plan, and the fear of letting my colleagues and supervisor down. I don't experience this kind of anxiety in my personal relationships or my social life outside of work at all. It's really just concentrated on my job and trying to keep up.

Can you think of any situations or times when you felt this level of anxiety or dread before your promotion to the client-facing sales strategist role, or is this experience entirely new to you since taking on that position?

This intense level of dread and anxiety is entirely new to me; before the promotion, my informal systems worked well enough to maintain my reputation for calm competence. While I had some struggles in childhood, like daydreaming in school or wandering off from chores, I never felt this overwhelming panic about my performance. It was only after those coping systems failed in this new role that the anxiety really took over.

You mentioned not avoiding tasks but dreading going into the office; can you elaborate on whether there are any specific work-related situations or tasks that you find yourself avoiding or putting off due to feelings of anxiety or being overwhelmed?

I don't actually avoid starting my tasks, and in fact, I work late hours trying to stay on top of them. The overwhelm happens when I try to organize; I'll stare at my campaign lists unable to decide what to tackle first, or get distracted mid-task and leave things half-finished. My dread is really about the constant anxiety of letting people down and being on a performance plan, rather than avoiding the work itself.
Can you describe if there are any specific thoughts or memories that trigger your anxiety, or if it's more related to the anticipation of potential failures or negative outcomes in your work?

It is definitely more about the anticipation of potential failures and making mistakes. While the recent negative feedback from my supervisor is a painful memory, the primary driver is the constant, daily dread of failing to keep up with my campaigns. Being on the performance plan just makes me constantly worry that I'm going to miss a key detail or let everyone down again.

Can you think of any situations at work where you feel like you're able to manage your tasks and anxiety without feeling overwhelmed, or are there specific aspects of your job that you feel you handle well despite your current struggles?

Honestly, I can't think of any aspect of my current strategist role that I'm handling well right now, as the overwhelm feels pretty constant across all of my tasks. I used to feel much more in control in my previous, execution-focused support role before the promotion, but now everything just feels completely out of my hands.
Is there anything that suggests your anxiety might be related to a specific traumatic event or a significant change in your life outside of the promotion and work performance issues you've described?

No, there are no traumatic events or other major life changes outside of work that I can think of. My personal life has been completely stable, so all of this stress is purely tied to the promotion and my performance struggles at the office.

Can you confirm whether your anxiety and feelings of overwhelm are exclusively related to your work performance and the fear of letting others down, or if there are any underlying fears or worries about your own well-being or safety that might also be contributing to your anxiety?

Yes, my anxiety is completely tied to my work performance and the fear of letting my team and supervisor down on this performance plan. I don't have any underlying worries about my physical safety or personal well-being outside of this professional stress. It's strictly about trying to keep up with my job.

Can you tell me if you have experienced any significant anxiety or distress when you are not able to control or prepare for a situation, such as an unexpected meeting or a sudden change in plans, outside of your work context?

I haven't really noticed any significant anxiety or distress about unexpected changes or a lack of control outside of work. My main struggles are really just focused on keeping my projects organized and managing my daily tasks at my job. Outside of my office environment, those kinds of situations don't really bother me.

Can you describe how your anxiety and feelings of overwhelm change when you are working on tasks that are within your control and have a clear structure, versus tasks that are more open-ended or unpredictable?

When tasks have a clear structure and are execution-focused—like in my old sales support role—I feel calm, reliable, and in control using my own informal systems. But with open-ended or unpredictable tasks, like mapping out complex campaigns now, I get highly anxious, stare at my to-do lists without knowing where to start, and end up bouncing aimlessly between projects feeling completely out of control.

Can you confirm if there are any periods, even brief, where you feel completely free from anxiety and dread related to your work performance, or is this feeling of being 'on edge' constant, even on weekends or days off?

It's really hard to completely shake the feeling because the worry about unfinished tasks and the upcoming week usually hangs over me. I'm not entirely sure if I ever feel completely free of it, or if it's truly constant on my days off, but it definitely lingers in the background.
Are there any specific aspects of your work, such as public speaking, meetings, or specific tasks, that trigger your anxiety more than others, or is it more the overall pressure of your role?

It’s really a combination of both; the overall pressure of being on a performance improvement plan and working late every night creates a constant background stress. However, I also have specific triggers, like long client meetings where sitting still makes me feel like I'm crawling out of my skin, and team meetings where waiting my turn to present makes me incredibly anxious and impatient.

Can you distinguish whether your anxiety is more about the fear of failing in your role, the fear of negative evaluation by others, or the inability to cope with the workload itself, as this might help clarify the underlying issue driving your symptoms?

To be honest, those three things feel deeply interconnected rather than separate. It started with my inability to cope with the heavy workload and cognitive load of organizing these complex campaigns, which led to missed deadlines and being placed on a performance plan, triggering a severe fear of failing. That failure directly feeds into my fear of negative evaluation, because losing my reputation as a quiet, reliable professional and feeling like I'm constantly letting my supervisor and team down is incredibly distressing.
Can you describe how you typically cope with anxiety and feelings of overwhelm in your daily life, and whether these coping mechanisms have changed since you started experiencing these symptoms?

To cope, I try to overcompensate by working late into the night and using a massive array of tools like sticky notes, color-coded calendars, and multiple to-do apps. Since my promotion, though, these methods have become exhausting and completely ineffective. I just end up staring at my lists, bouncing between tasks, and re-reading documents late at night without ever feeling in control.

Can you further clarify if there's any aspect of your work performance anxiety that you feel is not directly related to the fear of letting others down or failing in your role, such as anxiety triggered by the work environment itself or specific tasks that you find inherently stressful?

While the fear of letting people down is huge, there are definitely specific tasks and environments that cause intense stress on their own. For instance, trying to organize or map out campaigns makes me feel completely overwhelmed and paralyzed just looking at my lists. Also, sitting still through long client meetings or trainings makes me feel extremely restless, like I'm crawling out of my skin and need to find any excuse to get up.
Can you tell me if there are any moments or situations where you feel like you're completely unable to escape or control your anxiety, even when you're trying to use your usual coping mechanisms?

I wouldn't say I experience that kind of intense, uncontrollable anxiety or panic. While I feel highly stressed, frustrated, and overwhelmed by my disorganization and work performance, it doesn't really manifest as an inability to control anxiety itself. It is more of a constant, exhausting struggle to keep my focus and tasks under control.

Can you think of any situations where your anxiety significantly improves or worsens when you're able to implement your usual coping mechanisms, such as using your to-do lists or color-coded calendars, versus when you're unable to use them?

Even when I try to use my color-coded Google calendar, sticky notes, and to-do apps, they don't actually relieve my anxiety or help me feel in control. In fact, staring at those lists often makes me feel even more overwhelmed because I can't figure out where to start. I just end up bouncing between tasks and feeling completely out of control late into the night.

Can you describe how your anxiety and feelings of overwhelm would change if you were to return to a role with less complexity and fewer responsibilities, similar to your previous position before the promotion?

Returning to a role like my old sales support position would honestly bring immense relief and lower my anxiety, since my informal systems actually worked back then when I didn't have to juggle complex campaigns. While it would ease the overwhelming pressure of constantly falling behind, it also feels really discouraging to think about taking a step backward after working so hard for the promotion.
Can you describe any situations or tasks outside of work where you find yourself avoiding or procrastinating due to feelings of anxiety or being overwhelmed, similar to how you feel at the office?

I haven't really noticed this happening as much in my personal life. Right now, all of my energy and focus are so consumed by my struggles at work that I haven't really paid attention to how I'm managing tasks outside of the office.

Can you tell me if there's a specific point at which you feel like your anxiety and overwhelm become unbearable, such as when you're given a new task or when you realize you've missed a deadline, and how you typically react in those moments?

The overwhelm really peaks when I try to map out my campaigns and just stare at my lists, completely unable to decide where to start, or when I realize I've missed a detail and fallen behind. When that happens, I react by bouncing aimlessly between projects and staying up late re-reading the same planning documents over and over without absorbing anything. It leaves me feeling this deep sense of dread and distress because I feel like I'm constantly letting everyone down.

Can you describe how your anxiety and feelings of overwhelm might change if you were able to successfully implement a highly structured and organized system for managing your work tasks, potentially with the help of a professional organizer or coach?

If a structured system actually worked, it would be an immense relief and would take away a huge portion of the anxiety and dread I feel about going to work. But I've tried so many calendars and apps that just fall apart, leaving me staring at lists in a freeze, so I feel pretty exhausted and skeptical. While a coach sounds amazing, I’m so overwhelmed right now that even the idea of setting up another new system feels completely daunting.
